title: Worst update ever
body: I have been a long time Cook’n user. Before this update it was so seamless to copy a recipe from online and paste it directly into the app. Because of this update, the format to every recipe I have is messed up, and requires me to manually input every single ingredient instead of just copy and paste. This has turned a usual 1 minute process into 5 minutes of manual input per recipe. I won’t be using Cook’n anymore.

title: Holding recipes hostage
body: Been a free subscriber to this app for over six years. All of a sudden I can’t access my recipes unless I pay $4.99 to download them. Ridiculous!

title: Lost all my recipes
body: I have lost all my recipes after the launch/reboot issue the app just had. I have been storing these for years and now some of our family favorite recipes are gone. This is the worst app ever!

title: stopped working
body: After 2 days and maybe 5 recipes added it just stopped working - would not open and said “no internet” which was not accurate. This app is garbage. Don’t waste your time.

title: Overpriced and over hyped
body: The scanning function is pretty inaccurate, I have had much better luck with Recipe Bro (free). There are ads in the suggested recipes feed, if I want that I will go to Pinterest. And they seem to think we want to pay for a social media experience, no thanks. The basic plan does not offer support, why would I pay for an app with no support? Update regarding the developer’s response: I stand by my review re scanning accuracy and support. I have currently scanned over 100 recipes with Recipe Bro and have never had to edit even one, and this even includes handwritten recipes from old recipe cards. For recipes with handwritten notes, it scans the note along with the recipe. Their AI scanning technology is phenomenal. The developer of Cook’n needs to check his competition before being so defensive about the quality of his product. I have no connection to the developers of Recipe Bro. Also, I found two minor bugs when using Recipe Bro and they were very responsive, issuing a fix in less than one day. For a fraction of the price of Cook’n, the support was amazing.

title: Very MAGA Friendly
body: The app is great but I would not recommend any subscription services. Very right leaning views in their newsletter.

title: Deleted my recipes

I liked this app because I could scale the recipe up and down depending on how many people I was feeding. Well, I just opened this app, because I’m throwing a pizza party, only to find out Cook n’ went to a BS cloud subscription model, but, hey!, you can download your existing recipes locally for $4.99. Thanks for the ransomware, guys. Now my two recipes are gone. DONT USE THIS APP! The devs lack integrity.

title: The WORST cookbook software
body: If you are looking to create a cookbook, this software is the actual WORST way to do it. After pouring hours of work into adding recipes, you're left with the ugliest choices of themes to format your book & out $100+ for the software.. not to mention the cost of the actual cookbooks. It is beyond frustrating to work with on the computer and the app. Cook'n, you caused multiple family fights & hours of frustration! Good riddance.

title: Worst app ever
body: I stored all my recipes in here for years and then one day it all erased and said if I wanted it it would charge me so I lost everything. Don’t ever get this app.

title: No stars.
body: They changed the app and now my recipes are gone. All of them. Even my mother’s chili recipe. I can’t contact support unless I upgrade and pay to be a premium user. DO NOT PUT YOUR RECIPES ON HERE OR YOU RISK LOSING THEM!

title: Bait and Charge
body: Looks like a free app (in exchange for enduring ads). You get a month to add your recipe and become otherwise invested and then even the most basic functions require a monthly subscription fee on minimum of $5/month. Pretty deceptive and not appreciated.

title: I loved it initially
body: The ads for a paid membership have become ridiculous. In the last year, every recipe I save, I have to sit through an at least 30 second ad begging me to buy a membership. An occasional ad would be ok. Today, as I was cooking, cocktails g, and vibing on ITunes, the obnoxious ads hit. Every touch of the IPad set off an ad telling me how great a monthly membership is - along with videos of the owner’s family ski vacations in the Alps or Aspen,or wherever it was. Funding other people’s’ family holidays has never been enough for me to buy a membership to a website. Since the bulk of my saved recipes come from another site, I’m more likely to just save and subscribe there. Overall, it wouldn’t be a bad website. They need to move beyond the over.y obnoxious hustling for subscriptions if they want to make it last and work. I myself, have lost patience with it… Developer response was bordline insulting. Won’t recommend. Deleting app immediately.

title: Be careful

I tried logging in every way I could possibly have done in the past, even though I knew I had not had previously. Everything was gone! In my opinion this is a crappy app!

title: Disappointing….Don’t bother!!! Your recipe’s will disappear
body: I’ve had this app for a couple years and had loaded and shared many of my personal recipes only to find they are all gone and if you’re not a premium paying member, they do not support you. Disappointing

title: Trying to contact them is impossible!

title: Live links?

I tried storing one in the comments section of a newly added recipe, but it stores only as plain text, not an active link. Is this capability available here and I just haven’t discovered it? I began asking this question via their support option, but apparently they only reply to paid subscribers, and I’m certainly not going to subscribe to something before I determine that it fulfills my needs.

title: Not worth the time
body: App pushes to upgrade constantly (approx every other recipe you look at). Does not scan about half of the recipes found online. Monthly fee of either $4.99, $9.99, or $14.99 depending on what level you choose. Find an app that only charges a one time fee for unlimited recipes.

title: Disappointed

I thought I found something to share with my daughters. You can only do that if you are a member. I don’t want to pay for anything. I just want to share with my daughters. When I try to capture a recipe, I am given a screen that encourages me to sign up for a membership which I have done several weeks ago. I am very frustrated with the app and wish it could be fixed so it worked properly fixed.

title: Don't recommend

Six months later I now get an email they're going to delete everything unless I pay $5/month. Wish I never would have found this app.

title: Do not buy
body: I downloaded this app years ago. I clicked on the app and it says I need to subscribe. I was not able to access any of my recipes. It is free to download but you have to pay to do absolutely anything. There are physical cook books you can write in, and other apps that are actually free to use. The actual app was terrible the last time I used it.

title: Free is now less than useless
body: I have used this app for a long time. Years, in fact. I spent the money on the subscription for a year, and as far as I could tell - getting to upload more than 5 recipes per day (at the time) was the only real benefit to me. So, I dropped the subscription. I have told a number of friends and relatives about this app, because it seems to work just like I want it to. But, for some reason, when my friends and relatives sign up for an account now, they get video ads when searching for new recipes that last long enough that it is faster to not use that “discover” part of the app. They also cannot share their cookbooks with me even though I can share mine with them for some reason. The developer was onto something really good, but it seems he is more interested in responding with snide and petty comments to reviews over spending time developing a really good product with a useful subscription price point. It’s a shame. So much potential. I suppose if one doesn’t mind watching video commercials every time you are looking for a new recipe, and you never want to share your cookbook access with anyone else - including your spouse in your own home - this app could still be useful.

title: Ads Ads Ads
body: Looking for a new recipe app, downloaded this and could barely look at a recipe without multiple pop up ads. Uninstalled

title: Forced payments
body: I had been using this app for a long time without issue and really enjoyed keeping my recipes here. Then they changed how they work, and decided to switch to monthly subscription service. Without warning, I couldn’t even log in to see my existing recipes without erasing my data in favor of the cloud storage and signing up for a paid monthly subscription. The app isn’t advanced enough to be worth paying money every month - I already have recipe cards for free and easy reference.

title: Crashes and Annoying Ads
body: Update: Developer says it’s “impossible” that their app is crashing, so clearly I must be lying. Why would I lie about your app crashing? I have no skin in the game. I am a frustrated user who wanted to find a decent recipe organizer better than Pinterest. I was hoping to possibly recommend it to my team of volunteers who are compiling a community fundraiser cookbook. You made it quite clear that there was NO app support unless the user pays for a subscription. I went to your website to try to figure out a way to do so, even! And as for the sound issue, the issue is with the sound playing when the phone is in “silent mode”, not with the sound turned off. Maybe you should talk to the folks at Apple to figure out how to stop your ads from blaring when the phone is switched to silent. You know that little switch on the side that turns off the ringer? And while I’m not a developer, I do know that switching this off can silence ads in other apps, without turning the volume down to zero. I use a lot of apps that have ads that don’t have sound when I use silent mode. I’ve tested it! I have no problems watching a few ads to support a free app. I just don’t want the sound to suddenly blare when I’m next to my sleeping partner or child. There is no way I would ever sign up to pay for an app with a developer who responds in such an accusatory and rude manner. Downgrading to 1 out of 5 stars. App crashes constantly, even after several updates in the short time that I’ve been using. When it isn’t crashing, it interrupts periodically with annoying ads that use sound, even on silent mode (my partner trying to sleep next to me), that try to get you to sign up for a subscription. Why the heck would I sign up for a subscription when the app is constantly crashing during the short time (2 weeks) that I’ve been trying to use it. And stop annoying me to rate your app! Here’s your rating. I honestly kept hoping for the best, that you would fix whatever was making it crash, but it’s not to be.

title: Love the app - just wish it weren’t so expensive
body: I used Living Cookbook for years - even continued using it when the creators disappeared. However, I knew I needed something to replace it before it went down and I lost hundreds of recipes, and I have continued to look over the years. Recently I discovered Cook’n and overall I’m impressed. There are some things I’m not enthusiastic about - such as the ugly interface on my Windows PC or the fact that I can’t do certain things on my tablet or phone and have to go to the laptop (for instance, it would be really nice to be able to pull up my meal plan every day on my phone instead of printing it out from the laptop, which I don’t have room for in the kitchen). I could even see paying $150 for a premium membership plan if it were good for more than a year, but to pay $150 every year (or $180 if I go with a monthly pay plan) is really hard to swallow. Ever since my trial week ran out I’ve been debating on what membership plan to get. I’d gladly buy the Standard plan if it weren’t for those annoying adds every time I add a recipe because I don’t care about the cookbooks and have no idea exactly what the AI does, but it seems the only way to prevent those ads is with the Premium membership. UPDATE: received a response from Cook’n support and it seems the ads are removed with a standard member, which is more in line with my budget. When you look at the features of the different membership plans the only one checked for “No Ads” is the premium version. As soon as my free trial ended I started getting a pop up ad every time I added a new recipe, which was driving me crazy. But if the standard membership removes those, then that makes me happy. Since leaving my initial review I’ve been looking at tutorials and it seems the Cook’n team are constantly looking at improvements, so a yearly membership does make sense. One thing that I never did see anywhere and only discovered when I bought the Premium membership for a month is that you cannot upgrade to the latest version (without paying for it) unless you purchase a yearly membership. I bought the monthly and then realized that I was running a version much older than the latest, and was told after I’d pad 5 months in a row I could upgrade.

title: Best Recipe Organizer Out There
body: Over the years I've compiled many of my own family recipies and was looking for a place to put them. The problem with a traditional cookbook is that our recipes evolve. I am constantly experimenting with recipes so my personal cookbook is constantly changing, something that doesn't work very well with a paper cookbook. So I wanted something that would allow me to edit my recipes as I change them and always add new recipes to it. Pros: - The recipe scanner is really convenient to import photos from a physical page - Personal cookbooks can be made and recipies organized into chapters - Unlimited recipies stored to device - Print recipies as an organized sheet Cons: - I didn't realize at first that there was a premium version and you start on the free trial and after a few days you loose access to some features such a syncing with the cloud - Adds get really repetitive - No lifetime premium purchase option Conclusion: Although I was sad to see some things go when the trial expired, and I have no interest in paying $5/month for full access to my own recipes (because I'm not interested in exploring other recipes), it's still far better than any other app I've tried, and I've tried probably 10-15 different apps.

title: I lost years of recipes! 😢
body: I had enjoyed using the free version of this app for years. It’s a wonderful app. I had loaded hundreds of recipes, including recipes of my mom’s who is no longer with us. Oct. 18th the app kept freezing & wouldn’t load. I deleted & reinstalled it, but I lost everything & they are no longer available for me to recover. I am heart broken!! 😢 *Updated my review after communicating with Customer Service & Dan* I contacted Cook’n. Their customer service department & Dan were very helpful in explaining a few things that I wish I had realized/understood before. So I’ll share it with you, so you do not experience what I have went through. Even though I used the free version, I now understand that periodically I should have paid the subscription fee of $4.95 so my recipes could sync up to the cloud, & then cancel the subscription within 30 days (before the next month’s charge). This would have insured that my recipes would have been saved & easily accessible even if I had to delete & reinstall the app, or got a new phone for whatever reason. So I suggest if you use this app that you either pay the monthly subscription fee, periodically pay $4.95 to upload your recipes to the cloud, or make sure that you keep hard copies of all your recipes in case the app freezes & wont load, or your phone malfunctions … or your beloved recipes will be gone forever 😢

title: Cook’n App The digital kitchen appliance you didn’t know you needed!
body: We have used this app on our phones, tablets, and computers for quite some time. We use it daily for meal planning and to save favorite recipes. Our “Friends” encompass not only family but close associates and all love the ease of searching for favorites as well as adding new recipes to share and try! We also easily share recipes by email or text messages. The attention to comparability is evident in the cross platform utility, (we are waiting for a better ‘Safari’ browser plug-in and “177 Milk Street” capture functionality 🤔). Milk Street embeds so much content that I imagine it is quite challenging to develop a means to capture. That being said it isn’t that difficult to manually copy and paste their recipes! One caveat, it takes some planning to embed a recipe into another. Once you get the hang of it you will find that you use that function often! We have also used this App for grocery lists as well as occasional meal planning. We often shop for bargains and then browse our personal recipes for suitable use. This App is a bargain. It is easy to use and we have collected many new favorites as well as preserved family recipes that would have been lost. We recommend it for all, even a casual use will have you relying on Cook’n! We have a dedicated ancient iPad that sits proudly in the kitchen ready to display today’s dinner.

title: Overall a really good app, some new features/fixes would make it great
body: First, I do want to give 5 stars and a shoutout to tech support guy Matthew. I had some strange issues with syncing, and with the Mac app, and he kept with me until it was fixed! Having used another app for many years (which unfortunately the developer stopped supporting) I do compare Cook’n to the old app. Small things like: - Being able to select ingredients to add to shopping list (vs adding all, when many of them I have at home) - Enabling me to use the scan recipe without having to scan (I now scan a picture with one word on it and then copy and paste ingredients into that tool as a work around, and then highlight name, ingredients, directions etc. - Change the number of servings (and adjust ingredients) without saving recipe (make saving with new servings optional) -Fix issue where if you are using grams for weights and you change number servings (to half the recipe, for ex), that the ingredients in grams adjust properly (they convert to incorrect lbs now) Update: thanks for the response. I had reported the issue ( iOS Support [#3722]) with grams and changing the servings (it is a bug) a month ago, but have not heard back from the developer on this (Matthew forward to the developers on 4/17/20) On the scanning. I was not clear in my comment. I am wanting to use Cook’n on iOS (iPad) to copy recipes from another iOS app into Cook’n- I do not have the original sources. The iPad app has scan recipe tool, which once you have scanned something works like the snip-it tool on the Mac (highlight name, description, ingredients etc), but requires that you scan something first. I tried to take a picture of the screen in the original iPad app, but the scan tool is not very reliable for those images, so made more work for me. I have figured out by accident that if I tap scan recipe in iOS iPad app, then tap “Clear selection”, it does not make me put in an image, and I can copy and paste recipes from my old app into the Cook’n scan tool. For me, this works for my copy/paste (aka snip-it) needs, but is a work around I discovered, vs an intentional feature that I wanted!

body: I bought Cook’n when it first was debuted and converted all my recipes from MasterCook. Was a chore back then to type in some of the recipes, then be able to find them. Their technical support department receives a score of 100+ for responding via email until we got the issue resolved. I use Cook’n on my MacBook, my iPad, and iPhone and all my recipes and meal plans sync amongst all the devices.
